                                  13           Having received no summary judgment motion by the April 21, 2026 deadline, the Court

                                  14   SETS the following deadlines in this matter.1

                                  15   I.      TRIAL DATE

                                  16           A.         Jury trial remains set for December 1, 2026, at 8:30 a.m., in Courtroom 10, 19th

                                  17   Floor, U.S. District Court, 450 Golden Gate, San Francisco, California.

                                  18           B.         The Court expects the length of the trial to not exceed 3 court days, including jury

                                  19   selection.2

                                  20   II.     PRETRIAL CONFERENCE

                                  21           A.         A final pretrial conference is re-set for November 4, 2026, at 11:00 a.m., in

                                  22   Courtroom 10, 19th Floor. Lead trial counsel for each party shall attend.

                                  23           B.         By no later than September 28, 2026, the parties shall do the following:

                                       30, but three days should be more than sufficient given the nature of the case.

                                   8   list for its case-in-chief witnesses (including those appearing by deposition), including, for all such

                                   9   witnesses (other than party plaintiffs or defendants), a short statement of the substance of his/her

                                  10   testimony and, separately, what, if any, non-cumulative testimony the witness will offer. For each

                                  11   witness, state an hour/minute time estimate for the direct examination (only). Items (d) and (e)

                                  12   should be submitted as appendices to the proposed order. The proposed order should also state

                                  21   Instruction No. ____ Re ____________ Offered by _________________,” with the blanks filled

                                  22   in as appropriate. All disputed versions of the same basic instruction shall bear the same number.

                                  23   Any modifications to a form instruction must be plainly identified. If a party does not have a

                                       examination of the other side’s case-in-chief (other than for impeachment). Defense witnesses are

                                       pursuant to Paragraph II.B are waived.

                                  13                  5.      File trial briefs on any controlling issues of law.

                                  14                  6.      File proposed verdict forms, joint or separate.

                                  15                  7.      File and serve any objections to exhibits.

                                  16                  8.      File a joint simplified Statement of the Case to be read to the jury during

                                  17   voir dire as part of the proposed jury instructions. Unless the case is extremely complex, this

                                  18   statement should not exceed one page.

                                  19                  9.      File a joint statement listing the people involved in the case. This list will

                                  20   be shown to prospective jurors during jury selection. The list should include counsel, the parties,

                                  21   the potential witnesses, and any other people significantly involved in the case.

                                  22          C.      Any motions in limine shall be submitted as follows. By September 28, 2026, the

                                  23   moving party shall serve, but not file, the opening brief. By October 5, 2026, the responding

                                  24   party shall serve the opposition. There will be no reply. When the oppositions are received, the

                                  25   moving party should collate the motion and the opposition together, back-to-back, and then file

                                  26   the paired sets by noon on October 6, 2026. Each motion should be presented in a separate

                                  27   memorandum and properly identified, for example, “Plaintiff’s Motion in Limine No. 1 to

                                  28

                                         Case 4:24-cv-06777-AMO             Document 42         Filed 04/30/26     Page 4 of 9




                                   1   Exclude . . . .” Each side is limited to bringing five motions in limine. Each motion should

                                   2   address a single, separate topic, and contain no more than seven pages of briefing per side.

                                   3           D.      Two paper courtesy copies of the above documents shall be delivered by NOON

                                   4   the day after filing. The Joint Proposed Final Pretrial Order, jury instructions, and verdict form

                                   5   shall also be submitted via e-mail as separate attachments to AMOpo@cand.uscourts.gov. The

                                   6   Court requests that all hard-copy submissions be three-hole-punched, double-sided, and in a

                                   7   binder with tabs indicating the name of the document and corresponding docket number.

                                   8   III.    DEPOSITION AND DISCOVERY DESIGNATIONS

                                   9           Unless otherwise ordered, by no later than November 17, 2026, the parties shall jointly file

                                  10   all designations of deposition testimony or other discovery it wishes to offer, as well as any

                                  11   counter-designations or objections to the deposition testimony or discovery offered by any other

                                  12   party. There is no need to lodge deposition transcripts before trial. The lawyers should simply be
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   prepared to hand to the Court a copy of a witness’s deposition testimony once it is time to cross-

                                  14   examine them.

                                  15   IV.     PRETRIAL ARRANGEMENTS

                                  16           A.      Should a daily transcript and/or real-time reporting be desired, the parties shall

                                  17   make arrangements with Melinda Lock, Supervisor of the Court Reporting Services, at (415) 522-

                                  18   3149, at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the trial date.

                                  19           B.      During trial, counsel may wish to use overhead projectors, laser-disk/computer

                                  20   graphics, poster blow-ups, models, or specimens of devices. Equipment should be shared by all

                                  21   counsel to the maximum extent possible. The Court provides no equipment other than an easel.

                                  22   The United States Marshal requires a court order to allow equipment into the courthouse. For

                                  23   electronic equipment, parties should be prepared to maintain the equipment or have a technician

                                  24   handy at all times. The parties shall tape extension cords to the carpet for safety. The parties may

                                  25   work with the deputy clerk, Alexis Solorzano-Rodriguez, at 415-522-2030, on all courtroom-

                                  26   layout issues, which should be finalized at least ten (10) calendar days prior to the trial date.

                                  27

                                  28
                                                                                           4
                                         Case 4:24-cv-06777-AMO               Document 42       Filed 04/30/26    Page 5 of 9




                                   1          C.      By no later than November 17, 2026, the parties must provide the Court Reporter a

                                   2   jointly-created list of names and places as well as any uncommon terms or acronyms that are

                                   3   likely to come up during the trial.

                                   4   V.     SCHEDULING

                                   5          Trial will be conducted from 8:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m., depending on the availability of

                                   6   witnesses and jurors, Tuesday – Friday, with two 10-minute breaks each day. The Court will be

                                   7   dark on Mondays to accommodate its criminal calendar. Counsel must arrive by 8:15 a.m., or

                                   8   earlier as needed, for any matters to be heard out of the presence of the jury. The jury will be

                                   9   called at 8:30 a.m.

                                  10   VI.    THE JURY

                                  11          The Jury Office asks prospective jurors to complete an online jury questionnaire in

                                  12   advance of their summons date. The standard questionnaire is available on the Northern District’s
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   website at http://www.cand.uscourts.gov/wp-content/uploads/attorneys/Internet-version_Standard-

                                  14   CAND-Trial_SurveyMonkey_3-2022.pdf. The parties are allowed to propose 10 case specific

                                  15   questions to add to the questionnaire. The parties shall meet and confer, and to the extent

                                  16   possible, file a joint list of proposed questions to add to the questionnaire. To the extent that the

                                  17   parties cannot agree, they may file separate proposed questions from which the Court will choose

                                  18   an appropriate number. The parties’ joint or separate submissions should be filed by October 6,

                                  19   2026, with a Word version of the filed version emailed to AMOpo@cand.uscourts.gov. The

                                  20   parties need not include a question that asks prospective jurors whether they know any of the

                                  21   individuals involved in the case. The prospective jurors will be given an “Involved Individuals”

                                  22   list when they are called in. The Court will provide the parties with the survey responses the

                                  23   Friday before trial.

                                  24          In civil cases, there are no alternate jurors and the jury is selected as follows: Eighteen to

                                  25   twenty jurors are called to fill the jury box and the row in front of the bar, and are given numbers

                                  26   (1 through 20). The remaining potential jurors will be seated in the public benches. Hardship

                                  27   excuses will usually be considered at this point. Counsel may conduct a limited voir dire.

                                  28   Challenges for cause will then be addressed out of the presence of the potential jurors. The Court
                                                                                           5
                                         Case 4:24-cv-06777-AMO            Document 42         Filed 04/30/26      Page 6 of 9




                                   1   will consider whether to fill in the seats of the stricken jurors. If so, questions will be asked of the

                                   2   additional jurors and cause motions as to them will be considered. After a short recess, each side

                                   3   may exercise its allotment of peremptory challenges out of the presence of the potential jurors.

                                   4   The eight (or such other size as will constitute the jury) surviving the challenge process with the

                                   5   lowest numbers become the final jury. If more (or fewer) than eight jurors are to be seated, then

                                   6   the starting number will be adjusted. The starting number will also be adjusted if the Court allows

                                   7   more than a total of six peremptories. Once the jury selection is completed, the jurors’ names will

                                   8   be read again and they will be seated in the jury box and sworn. The Court may alter this

                                   9   procedure in its discretion and after consultation with the parties.

                                  10   VII.   WITNESSES

                                  11          At the close of each trial day, all counsel shall exchange a list of witnesses for the next two

                                  12   full court days and the exhibits that will be used during direct examination (other than for
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   impeachment of an adverse witness). Within 24 hours of such notice, all other counsel shall

                                  14   provide any objections to such exhibits and shall provide a list of all exhibits to be used with the

                                  15   same witness on cross-examination (other than for impeachment). The first notice shall be

                                  16   exchanged prior to the first day of trial. All such notices shall be provided in writing and lodged

                                  17   with the Court.

                                  18          The parties shall have all upcoming witnesses on the same day available in the courthouse

                                  19   and ready to testify. Failure to have the next witness ready or to be prepared to proceed with the

                                  20   evidence will usually be deemed to constitute resting. If counsel plans to read in a transcript of a

                                  21   deposition, counsel must have a deposition prepared and vetted early on to read into the record.

                                  22          The parties are encouraged to stipulate where possible, for example, as to the exclusion of

                                  23   witnesses from the courtroom.

                                  24   VIII. EXHIBITS

                                  25            A.    Prior to the Final Pretrial Conference, counsel must meet and confer in person to

                                  26    consider all exhibit numbers and objections and to eliminate duplicate exhibits and confusion

                                  27    over the precise exhibit.

                                  28          B.      Use numbers only, not letters, for exhibits, preferably the same numbers as were
                                                                                          6

                                   3   exhibit should be marked only once. If the plaintiff has marked an exhibit, then the defendant

                                   4   should not re-mark the exact document with another number. Different versions of the same

                                   5   document, e.g., a copy with additional handwriting, must be treated as different exhibits with

                                   6   different numbers. To avoid any party claiming “ownership” of an exhibit, all exhibits shall be

                                   7   marked and referred to as “Trial Exhibit No. _____,” not as “Plaintiff’s Exhibit” or “Defendant’s

                                   1          E.      Before the closing arguments, counsel must confer with the deputy clerk to make

                                   2   sure the exhibits in evidence are in good order.

                                   3          F.      Exhibit notebooks for the jury will not be permitted without prior permission from

                                   4   the Court. Publication must be by poster blow-up, overhead projection, or such other method as is

                                   5   allowed in the circumstances. It is permissible to highlight, circle or underscore in the

                                   6   enlargements as long as it is clear that it was not on the original.

                                   7   IX.    OBJECTIONS

                                   8          In making objections, counsel should state only the legal grounds for the objection and

                                   9   should withhold all further comment or argument unless elaboration is requested by the Court.

                                  10   X.     CHARGING CONFERENCE

                                  11          As the trial progresses and the evidence is heard, the Court will fashion a comprehensive

                                  12   set of jury instructions to cover all issues actually being tried. Prior to the close of the evidence,
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   the Court will provide a draft final charge to the parties. After a reasonable period for review, one

                                  14   or more charging conferences will be held at which each party may object to any passage, ask for

                                  15   modifications, or ask for additions. Any instruction request must be renewed specifically at the

                                  16   conference or it will be deemed waived, whether or not it was requested prior to trial. If, however,

                                  17   a party still wishes to request an omitted instruction after reviewing the Court’s draft, then it must

                                  18   affirmatively re-request it at the charging conference, in order to give the Court a fair opportunity

                                  19   to correct any error. Otherwise, as stated, the request will be deemed abandoned or waived.

                                  20   XI.    TIME LIMITS

                                  21          In certain cases, the Court will set fixed time limits at the final pretrial conference. All of

                                  22   your examination time (whether direct, cross, re-direct or re-cross) for all witnesses and side bar

                                  23   conference time must fit within your time limit and you may allocate it as you wish. Opening and

                                  24   closing time limits shall be considered separately.

                                  25   XII.   NON-COMPLIANCE WITH PRETRIAL ORDER

                                  26          The parties are on notice that failure to comply with the requirements set forth in this order

                                  27   may result in sanctions, whether in the form of monetary sanctions, involuntary dismissal, or other

                                  28   appropriate order. While the parties may seek modest extensions of the deadlines set forth in this
                                                                                          8
                                         Case 4:24-cv-06777-AMO           Document 42        Filed 04/30/26    Page 9 of 9




                                   1   order, any request for an extension (whether by stipulation or administrative motion) must be filed

                                   2   at least seven days in advance of the deadline sought to be extended. Extensions that affect any

                                   3   dates on the Court’s calendar are unlikely to be granted.

                                   4          IT IS SO ORDERED.

                                   5   Dated: April 30, 2026

                                  14          On November 3, 2025, the Court issued an order granting in part and denying in part the

                                  15   parties’ joint stipulation to modify the case scheduling order. Dkt. No. 30 (“November 3 Order”).

                                  16   In the November 3 Order, the Court noted that although the parties reported completing private

                                  17   mediation on July 9, 2025, “their stipulation and supporting declaration ma[de] it clear that the

                                  18   parties engaged in that mediation without having conducted any of the discovery necessary to

                                  19   make it productive.” Id. at 2. The Court therefore ordered the parties to “schedule a further

                                  20   mediation session, to take place in February or March 2026.” Id. at 2. A notice confirming the

                                  21   scheduling of that session was due within 7 days of the November 3 Order. Id. at 2-3.

                                  22          To date, the required notice has not been filed. Accordingly, the parties are ORDERED

                                  23   TO SHOW CAUSE why they should not be sanctioned for failing to file the required notice.

                                  24   Each side shall file a response, not to exceed 3 pages, to this Order to Show Cause by March 6,

                                  25   2026. The Court notes that the prior $500 sanction imposed on Attorney David Lunn for not

                                  26   appearing at the status conference held July 16, 2025, Dkt. Nos. 24, 25, was insufficient to ensure

                                  27   Plaintiffs’ compliance with subsequent orders and deadlines. Accordingly, Plaintiffs are on notice

                                  28   that, should sanctions be warranted, the Court is inclined to impose a higher sanctions amount
